finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the 'f' query parameter is joined to /srv/files with filepath.Join, which cleans '..' segments but does not confine the result to the root. An attacker can read arbitrary files readable by the process.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter 'f' on GET /dl (files.go:12), unauthenticated
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, response written at files.go:18

trace.note: name taken directly from r.URL.Query().Get("f") with no validation
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd, which escapes root
file contents returned to the client

finding.guards_checked: No prefix check after Join, no filepath.Base, no allowlist, and no authentication or middleware (main registers the handler directly at files.go:32). The avatar handler uses filepath.Base, but download does not.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the raw 'f' query value into filepath.Join(root, name) with no prefix check, Base, or auth, so "../../etc/passwd" escapes /srv/files, and files.go:18 writes the contents back; files.go:32 registers the handler directly with no middleware.
